decisions.reason: As a newly launched sensor module with its own product page and a good fit to the firm's modular sensing platform, its performance is likely close enough to aspiration to justify continued support while demand becomes clearer.
Because this product is explicitly the new generation replacing an older voltage measurement module, it sits in an established product line and is therefore unlikely to be withdrawn soon.
The MQTT proxy extends the software ecosystem at relatively low carrying cost, so with organizational slack and strategic fit the firm would likely keep it unless results were clearly disappointing.
A CAN bus interface matches German industrial and automation use cases well, and despite lighter website emphasis its platform relevance makes retention more likely than withdrawal.

The CO2 sensor module broadens the sensing portfolio and had a dedicated page, but as a somewhat narrower and potentially more uncertain niche than core interface products it faces a moderately higher withdrawal risk.

The touch panel accessory is the most peripheral to the firm's core electronics and interface modules, so if early sales lag aspirations it is the most plausible candidate for reallocation of resources, though still more likely to be kept than dropped this soon after launch.
